title: What happened in AI — Nov 7, 2026
intro: Agent isolation led the day: a Firecracker rebuild of Google's microVM sandbox, Uber's agent security lessons, and Alex Stamos calling password access for agents 'insane' all point to per-session isolation and no standing credentials.
Tooling is catching up with testable skills and verification gates, including backend skills that cut critical mistakes from 25/150 runs to 2/150.
highlights: Firecracker rebuild of Google's agent sandbox publishes the latency numbers Google left out.
Uber details a distinct security model for agents that reason over untrusted content.
Alex Stamos: giving AI agents passwords is 'insane'.
APM brings one apm.yml dependency manifest to agent skills, prompts and MCP servers.
Backend skills cut critical mistakes from 25/150 to 2/150 runs in one benchmark.
TokiRecur reuses KV-cache prefixes to cut prefill cost in llama.cpp.

categories.name: Agent Sandboxing & Security
categories.summary: Isolation is the common answer: per-session microVMs, per-role containers, and no standing credentials for agents.

articles.title: Google Described Its Agent Sandbox. I Built One with Firecracker and Measured It
articles.summary: A Firecracker rebuild of Google's Agent Compute Engine design (microVM per session, copy-on-write clones from warm snapshots, no network card) supplies the latency numbers Google's post omitted.

articles.title: Securing AI Agents [at Uber]: Lessons from Real-World Deployment
articles.summary: Uber argues agents need a different security model than predefined-logic services because they reason over untrusted user and web content.

articles.title: Former Meta Security Chief Calls Password Access for AI Agents 'Insane'
articles.summary: Alex Stamos warns against handing agents passwords, as Meta ships custom 'spaces' in its Muse assistant.

articles.title: RigHaven – Self-hosted execution harness for AI agents
articles.summary: A coordinator composes role-based agent teams, each role in its own isolated container with access to 99 managed CLI tools.

categories.name: Agent Tooling & Skills
categories.summary: Skills, dependency manifests, and earned-autonomy gates are turning agent setup into something testable and reproducible.

articles.title: APM – A dependency manager for AI agents
articles.summary: Declare skills, prompts, instructions, plugins and MCP servers in one apm.yml; apm install deploys them to each supported harness, including GitHub Copilot.

articles.title: Show HN: Coding agent skills, tested on 15 backend tasks with hidden checks
articles.summary: Backend skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor cut critical mistakes from 25 of 150 runs to 2 of 150 in the author's tests.

articles.title: Show HN: Select – AI agents that earn autonomy through verified work

articles.title: Honeycomb Team Agents: AI SRE Done Right
